prize_parts.citation: For the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which a magic-wavelength optical lattice allows many neutral atoms to serve as a frequency reference with uncertainty near 1e-18

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from B028 to B048. The magic-wavelength lattice is a single, original concept, because it cancels the trapping light shift so that many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once. It was followed by decisive demonstrations, by Katori on the concept and first strontium realisation and by Ye on record accuracy and many-body regimes. It has been reproduced independently in many laboratories at uncertainties near 1e-18 and already supports comparisons of clocks, tests of constants and relativistic geodesy. It fits the criterion that the prize is for a discovery or invention rather than lifetime achievement, and it has a cleaner two-name attribution than any other shortlisted entry, including my own B028. I judged B028 on a field I know closely, and round 1 showed that this closeness was the main reason I kept it first. The nature of the invention and its mature, repeated demonstration are comparable, but B048 has the sounder credit and the wider scientific consequence.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for control of single quantum systems is real, and the citation must be worded as the lattice concept and its realisation, not as optical clocks in general. Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Bloom and the Paris and PTB groups fall outside a two-name credit, so the award is a judgment on credit and not a settled partition. The redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so part of the fundamental-physics payoff is still prospective. As an instrument builder I also see that B028 is arguably as mature and as routine in its use as B048, and that the committee passing over it leaves the 1986-to-now gap in electron microscopy unaddressed.

responses.point: The lattice clock is a single, well-defined invention with a clear chain from concept to 1e-18 results, and the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is the main risk, with a possible second part such as trapped-ion quantum logic.
responses.response: Stefan's argument that the lattice clock is a different concept, many atoms cancelling the trapping Stark shift, from the comb or single-ion control is what moved me most, since it answers the overlap objection on physical grounds and not by counting votes. I accept his 1e-18 clause in the citation as a way to anchor the invention to its demonstrated outcome. I do not support adding B003 as a second part. Nothing in round 1 makes it a natural pairing, and a second part would dilute a clean two-laureate case.

responses.point: Broad opening support is not itself evidence of merit and may only reflect the consensus safe option, but the lattice clock survives scrutiny on novelty, reproduction, consequences and attribution.
responses.response: I agree with Ulf that support counts cannot substitute for the science, and I tried to test this by asking whether I would still prefer B028 had it been ranked alongside the clock by everyone. I would not, because the clock's concept is more original and its credit more separable. His point about the overlap is the right test, and I find that the clock passes it, since the 2005 and 2012 prizes concern the comb and single-ion control and not a neutral-atom lattice with a cancelled light shift. I still share his worry that the credit is not exhaustive, and I would keep that in the record.

responses.point: As an experimentalist who builds instruments he values a measurement capability that someone had to invent and then drive to its systematic limit, and he thinks two names fit the statute without arbitrary exclusions.
responses.response: Mark's argument speaks to my own field as well, because a corrector is also an invention that had to be driven to its limit. That is why I do not treat instrument-enabling work as lesser, and why I no longer rank B028 above B048 on that criterion. The deciding difference is attribution, since his remark that the clock's credit divides without forcing arbitrary exclusions is not true of B028 once Krivanek and STEM correction are considered. I also accept that his Higgs alternative has a harder attribution problem than either of ours.

responses.point: Topological insulators with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp pair a Z2 theory prediction with experimental confirmation in HgTe and nearly two decades of independent confirmation.
responses.response: I still regard the Z2 theory and the HgTe experiment as a strong pairing, and I keep B019 as an alternative. I cannot make it my lead because the credit would omit Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who proposed the HgTe route, and the 2016 prize already covers topological phases. Olle's own caveat that the technological payoff is still prospective weighs more with me than the length of the confirmation record. If the committee sees the attribution as soluble, I would consider B019 for a later cycle.

uncertainties: Whether the citation can be worded to separate the lattice concept from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system prizes; I think it can, but this rests on drafting.
Whether Katori and Ye alone fairly cover the lattice clock given Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Bloom and the Paris and PTB groups; priority details rest on recollection and not on verified records.
Whether to act before the redefinition of the second; I lean toward acting now because the demonstrated science does not depend on the formal vote.
Whether a TEM-only credit for B028 could be defended against Krivanek and STEM correction in a later cycle.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My profile documents no personal tie to any credited person for B048, and I see no apparent conflict for it. I work in transmission electron microscopy and lead the international microscopy federation, so I may know Rose, Haider or Urban professionally, and I would recuse from B028 if the committee considers that a conflict; that is now only an alternative. Goran Johansson is also at Chalmers, with no apparent link to any shortlisted candidate. I have no apparent conflict for B019, B001, B054, B008, B003, B033, B036 or B052 from the provided profile.
